Erin —

Appreciate the clarity. Putting this together as a compact, auditable flow. Attached is a sample delta manifest and a signed stub bundle (signatures only; archive is a placeholder) we use in pilot runs. High level plan below, followed by the operator acceptance checklist (also attached).

High-level offline delta handshake (summary):
- Customer creates transfer media (USB-drive or encrypted SD) and copies: delta archive (.tar.gz), signature (.sig), manifest.json, and a transfer receipt (human-readable).
- Operator (on sealed site) verifies manifest hashes (SHA-256) against the archive, then verifies the signature using Redwood's public key (we'll share the key fingerprint separately).
- If signature verification passes, operator runs the integrity-only smoke test (container start with --dry-run) and records logs to the acceptance checklist.
- If smoke test passes, operator schedules staging window, applies delta to staging node, validates service-level smoke checks, then promotes to the rest of the cluster.

Operator acceptance checklist (high level):
1) Confirm physical custody control seals intact.
2) Verify manifest timestamp and delta sequence number.
3) Validate archive SHA-256 == manifest.record.archive_sha256.
4) gpg --verify signed-delta-bundle-v3.tar.gz.sig signed-delta-bundle-v3.tar.gz (instructions in attached checklist).
5) Run container dry-run: redwood-runtime --apply --dry-run --bundle ./delta.tar.gz > dryrun.log
6) Inspect dryrun.log for missing kernels/quant tables.
7) If dry-run OK, schedule staging window and apply to single node. Run smoke endpoints and perf sanity.
8) Upload acceptance checklist (scanned) and transfer receipt to your compliance bucket.

I've attached: delta-manifest-v1.json, signed-delta-bundle-v3.tar.gz.sig, operator-acceptance-checklist-20261207.xlsx (spreadsheet with checklist + expected pass/fail outcomes).

Quick notes on keying: we sign with our Redwood release signing key. For private deployments we support customer-managed verification via either: (A) Redwoods public verification key published to the customer's KMS fingerprint during onboarding, or (B) a mutually trusted intermediate signing key (customer generates, shares public key at onboarding). We'll share the key fingerprints and sample gpg commands in the onboarding doc.

I'll loop Karthik and Mina for rollout timing and on-site operator steps.

—Marissa

Redwood Inference
